transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I feel like I’m constantly worrying about money and my future, from the moment I wake up until I go to bed, and it’s taking over everything. It’s just gotten to the point where I feel completely overwhelmed and don't know how to make it stop.
Do you experience sudden, intense surges of fear or panic where your heart races and you feel like you might lose control, or is your worry more of a constant, lingering state throughout the day?

It is definitely more of a constant, lingering state throughout the day. It feels like there’s a low-grade alarm going off in my head all day, constantly jumping from one future worry to another. It's not a sudden surge of panic, just this nonstop, exhausting background noise.
Beyond these constant worries, have you noticed a persistent loss of interest or pleasure in the activities you usually enjoy, or do you feel a sense of emptiness or sadness?

Yes, I've really struggled to enjoy the things I used to love, like sitting in my garden or practicing the guitar, because I just end up repeatedly checking my bank account instead. It doesn't feel like a deep, empty sadness, but rather that my constant financial worry is completely crowding out my ability to relax and enjoy my hobbies.

If your financial worries were to suddenly resolve, do you feel your ability to enjoy your hobbies would return immediately, or do you feel a persistent sense of low mood or worthlessness even when you aren't actively worrying?

If those financial worries were resolved, I absolutely feel I’d be able to enjoy my hobbies again. It’s not that I feel worthless or deeply depressed; my mind is just so hijacked by checking my bank account and spinning out scenarios that I can't focus on anything else. If that constant mental alarm quieted down, I know I could get back to enjoying my guitar and garden.
Beyond the mental worry, have you been experiencing physical symptoms like muscle tension, restlessness, difficulty concentrating, or trouble falling or staying asleep?

Yes, I'm completely exhausted because I lie awake for hours running numbers and wake up at 3 AM unable to drift back off. My shoulders and neck constantly feel like I'm carrying a heavy backpack of rocks, and I'm clenching my jaw so hard my face aches. On top of that, my mind will just blank out in the middle of writing lesson plans or staff meetings because I'm so distracted.
How long have you been experiencing this constant, excessive worry and these physical symptoms on most days?

This constant, all-day worry has been my baseline for a little over a year now. It really escalated about a year after my divorce settlement, right around the time I started seriously planning my preschool venture and looking closely at my finances.
